article_title: GitHub Copilot Is Now Selectable in JetBrains Air for Local and Cloud Tasks on Copilot Plans; Air Neither Shows Copilot Usage Nor Caps Spending

content_preview.title: GitHub Copilot Is Now Selectable in JetBrains Air for Local and Cloud Tasks on Copilot Plans; Air Neither Shows Copilot Usage Nor Caps Spending
content_preview.summary: GitHub and JetBrains say Copilot can run in Air locally or in cloud sandboxes billed to Copilot plans, but Air does not track Copilot credits, show its usage or set spending limits.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub says developers can now use GitHub Copilot inside JetBrains Air. According to the [GitHub changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-github-copilot-is-now-available-in-jetbrains-air/), "you can now delegate coding tasks, guide execution, and review results with GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air," using the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) for tasks "in your JetBrains IDE or in the cloud." JetBrains published a companion post, [Use Your GitHub Copilot Plan in JetBrains Air](...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (770 words, within the 400-1200 range). Clear split between what each vendor says about local and cloud tasks, sandboxing, automations and usage/spending visibility; a Background section that dates the Register material; and a What We Don't Know section. Title is 143 characters (under 150, long but descriptive; its second clause is a sourced finding, not editorializing).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four gunzipped snapshots (source-0..3.html.gz, all HTTP 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all four, so no scanner findings to adjudicate). source-0 (GitHub Changelog, November 3, 2026): confirms 'You can now delegate coding tasks, guide execution, and review results with GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air', ACP, 'in your JetBrains IDE or in the cloud', the three What's new items including 'through Air Teams, from your IDE or browser' and 'rather than JetBrains AI credits', the three cloud requirements, the Docker-container/fresh-VM/proxy/no-state quote verbatim, and under 'Cloud task considerations' the subscription-check, plan-selection ('You cannot choose whether an individual task uses your personal ... or your organization's plan'), usage-visibility ('Air's governance and analytics features do not include Copilot usage') and administrative-controls ('can disable GitHub Copilot through a governance policy, but cannot set Copilot spending limits within Air') items. source-1 (JetBrains blog, Use Your GitHub Copilot Plan in JetBrains Air): confirms 'Tasks run on your existing Copilot plan, not on JetBrains AI credits', official Copilot CLI over ACP, same task list as Claude, Codex and Junie, no Air Teams needed locally but a Copilot subscription is, remote-branch requirement, Settings | VCS Providers sign-in via the GitHub connection, 'each run uses your Copilot plan', weekly dependency update recommendation, 'can drain your credits much faster, especially if the repository is busy', 'Air doesn't warn you when your credits are all used up - your runs will just start failing', and the FAQ quote 'Air doesn't track Copilot credits for local or cloud tasks, and it can't set a spending limit.' It also says 'Because Air doesn't show your Copilot usage and can't limit it', which is the vendor wording behind the title's second clause. source-2 (JetBrains blog, How Cloud-Based Agent Sandboxing Works in Air, October 2026 URL): confirms each task starts a VM, 'It is not reused between tasks', agent in a Docker container behind a proxy, default allowlist of 'trusted source control and package registry domains, such as npm', add domains / allow all / turn internet access off, microVMs 'coming soon', and 'Cloud agents are currently available to organizational users ... with a broader release for individual users planned later'. All sandboxing claims match. source-3 (The Register, Tue 10 Mar 2026): confirms public preview, Codex/Claude Agent/Gemini CLI/Junie, ACP 'which Zed and JetBrains sponsor', tasks in a local workspace, Git worktree, Docker or '(in a future release) a cloud container'. The article uses it only for the March launch and states in Background and What We Don't Know that it predates and does not address the integration; it is not used to support any integration claim. Allowlist: github.blog, blog.jetbrains.com and theregister.com are all already in config/source_allowlist.txt. Independent-source recount: 1 of 4 (The Register), independent of the vendors but covering only the March launch; the other 3 are first-party (GitHub, JetBrains x2). Not an Analysis, so no independence threshold applies; the article discloses that integration claims rest on vendor descriptions.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every quote checked against snapshots. One quote begins lowercase ('you can now delegate...') where the source sentence begins 'You can now delegate...'; this is a capitalisation-only change made so the quote runs into the article's sentence, and the quoted wording is otherwise verbatim, so it is acceptable and not a misquotation. Title: 'Now Selectable ... for Local and Cloud Tasks on Copilot Plans' matches both vendors (GitHub: 'Select GitHub Copilot and use your existing Copilot subscription'; JetBrains: 'You can now pick GitHub Copilot as the agent in Air - locally ... and in the cloud with Air Teams ... on your existing Copilot plan'). 'Air Neither Shows Copilot Usage Nor Caps Spending' is supported by JetBrains ('Air doesn't show your Copilot usage and can't limit it'; 'can't set a spending limit') and GitHub ('governance and analytics features do not include Copilot usage'; 'cannot set Copilot spending limits within Air'). The title does not drop a material qualifier: 'Copilot' scope is carried by the clause's subject matter, and the body states the cloud-task requirement (Air Teams business organization) that the title does not repeat. One subordinate inaccuracy found: the What We Don't Know bullet says 'both vendors direct users to GitHub for usage'. Only JetBrains does so ('Check your usage on GitHub'); the GitHub changelog contains no such direction. This sits in a limitations bullet, not the headline, summary or lead, and is recorded as a clarification. 'Every/each/all' statements hold (each Air task gets its own VM; each automation run uses the Copilot plan; both posts do list usage limits). Relative dates: none; dates are absolute (March, March 10).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributive throughout ('GitHub says', 'JetBrains says'); no promotional language or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Prior Herald coverage: 2026-10/05 (Air early access in IDEs), 2026-10/24 (Analysis on sandboxes), 2026-03/16 (Air launch); none covers the Copilot integration. Both internal links resolve to existing article files (/article/2026-10/05-jetbrains-opens-early-access... and /article/2026-10/24-sandboxes-and-permission-modes...) and are described accurately (News about early access; an Analysis). Added the March launch article as a related_articles entry in the article-meta file.
concerns: What We Don't Know says 'both vendors direct users to GitHub for usage'; only JetBrains' FAQ does, the GitHub changelog does not. Recorded as a clarification in the corrections record.
Title is 143 characters; under the 150 limit but long.
Single independent source (The Register) is relevant only to the March launch, so integration claims rest on vendor posts; the article discloses this.
recommendations: Attribute the 'direct users to GitHub for usage' statement to JetBrains alone.
Where possible seek independent testing or reporting on Copilot-in-Air credit consumption.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed News coverage of a defined-audience integration; all quotes, numbers, requirements and sandboxing details verified against the raw snapshots, with one minor limitations-bullet overreach handled by a clarification. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate, useful coverage of the Copilot-in-Air integration and its usage/spending visibility gaps for developers and teams using JetBrains Air
